children: The oil and gas industry launched a coordinated lobbying campaign to block a potential ban on U.S. diesel exports following proposal signals from President Donald Trump, warning that trade restrictions would spike domestic fuel prices, a media report said.

Shortly after Trump made his suggestion Tuesday, Mike Sommers, chief executive of the American Petroleum Institute, the industry’s top lobby, issued a statement condemning the move. He said restricting U.S. exports “would only compound the problem” of rising diesel costs. API also issued a press release on the dangers of an export ban.
Around the same time, a loose group of CEOs affiliated with API and the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, a trade group that represents refiners, sprang into action.
CEO Mark Lashier, and other senior executives started calling their contacts in the administration to push back on the idea of a ban, according to the
The executives have different relationships with different members of the administration, and they made their discontent known, the report said.
are among the other companies involved in the effort, according to people aware of the interactions. The industry has also been able to rely on Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas and Louisiana Republicans.

On Wednesday, more than 30 business, energy, and manufacturing groups, including API, AFPM, and the Business Roundtable, in a letter urged Trump to reject export restrictions. “While we understand the urge for a silver bullet, there are no easy answers,” the letter said, according to the

Oil lobbies and executives have been gearing up for a potential ban on energy exports since the beginning of the Iran war. They first anticipated restrictions on crude exports. Finally, it is diesel, whose price has exploded, that has become a target of the administration.

On Tuesday night, after U.S. oil executives relayed their fears to Trump officials, Energy Secretary Chris Wright called the CEOs of multiple U.S. oil companies and conveyed he favored a measure that would fall short of an export ban while satisfying Trump’s desire to lower diesel prices, the report added.

title: Big oil mobilizes to block Trump's diesel export ban idea: WSJ
